stem: In which year was the Regulating Act passed?
expl: To remove widespread corruption and misadministration in the Company, the British Parliament passed the Regulating Act, 1773. Under this, the Madras and Bombay Presidencies were brought under the Calcutta Presidency. The Governor of Bengal was now called the Governor-General of Bengal. Warren Hastings was made the first Governor-General of Bengal.

stem: Under which of the following acts did Lord Cornwallis get the right to overrule the decisions of his council?
expl: Cornwallis wanted to hold the powers of both the Governor-General and the Commander-in-Chief. According to the Act of 1786, this was accepted, and in special circumstances the Governor-General was also given the power to override the decisions of his Council and to enforce his own decision.

stem: When was the Pitt's India Act passed by the British Parliament?
expl: The Pitt’s India Act was passed in 1784 AD. The main provisions of the Pitt’s India Act, 1784 were the establishment of a Board of Control to supervise the Company’s civil, military and revenue affairs; reduction of the members of the Council of the Governor General in India to three members; and civil and military officers were asked to disclose details of their properties in India and Britain.

stem: Which Act provided for the competitive exam system for Civil Services?
expl: In the Charter Act, 1853, it was provided that the salaries of the Board of Control and its other officers would be fixed by the government; however, the Company would pay them. The number of Directors was reduced from 24 to 18, out of which 6 were to be nominated by the Crown. It also provided that appointments would now be made through competitive examinations, without any kind of discrimination.

stem: The post of the Indian High Commission was created by which Act?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In the Government of India Act, 1919, a provision was made for appointing an Indian High Commissioner to reduce the workload of the Secretary of State for India. Its functions included purchasing arms and other goods for the Government of India, awarding contracts, looking after commercial interests, and taking care of Indian students studying in England, etc. The expenditure on the salaries of the High Commissioner and his assistants was to be met from India’s resources.

stem: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report formed the basis of the–
expl: The report of Edwin Montagu (then Secretary of State for India) and Viceroy Lord Chelmsford became the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919. Under this Act, dyarchy was introduced in the provinces for the first time.

expl: In 1919, when the Montagu–Chelmsford Act was passed, David Lloyd George was the Prime Minister of the U.K. He remained the Prime Minister of the U.K. from 1916 to 1922.

stem: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as a ‘Charter of Slavery’?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In his presidential address at the annual session of the Congress held at Lucknow, on 12 April 1936, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru called the Government of India Act, 1935 the “Charter of Slavery.” This Act provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation in which both British Indian provinces and Indian States (Princely States) were to be included, though this federation could never actually come into existence. Under this Act, there was also a provision for a bicameral legislature at the Centre.

The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished provincial dyarchy and introduced provincial autonomy. As a result, the distinction between reserved and transferred subjects ended. With some reservations, responsible government was established in the provinces.

stem: Which of the following was not one of the features of the Government of India Act, 1935?

options.label: a
options.text: Reconstruction of the Governor General's Executive Council

expl: The features of the Government of India Act, 1935 included the proposal of an Indian Federation, reorganization of the Governor-General’s Executive Council, and provincial autonomy; however, there was no provision for an evaluation of the Act of 1935. This Act also provided for the establishment of a Federal Court, division of powers between the Centre and the Provinces, a bicameral Central Legislature, abolition of dyarchy in the provinces, and dyarchy at the Centre, etc. India’s present constitutional structure is largely based on the Act of 1935.

stem: Which Act provided for the partition of India into two new dominions -India and Pakistan?
expl: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, passed by the British Parliament, formally approved the partition of British India and provided the legal basis for the creation of two new independent dominions/states—India and Pakistan. This Act received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947, and it provided that from 15 August 1947 the two independent dominions/states India and Pakistan would come into existence.

stem: Who is considered the father of dyarchy?
expl: Sir Lionel Curtis is regarded as the father of dyarchy. His ideas related to dyarchy formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919.

stem: The Muddiman Committee was appointed to report on the working of which of the following?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Muddiman Committee was appointed in the year 1924 under the leadership of Sir Alexander Muddiman. This committee was appointed to discuss and examine the issue of dyarchy under the constitution established under the Government of India Act, 1919. Apart from the British members, it also had six Indian members—Shivswami Iyer, R. P. Paranjpye, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Bijoy/Vijay Chand Mahtab, Muhammad Shafi, and Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The committee submitted its report in the year 1925.
